my_sentences.en: look for vs. find
my_sentences.ko: look for는 찾는 과정(행위), find는 찾아낸 결과(발견)를 나타냅니다.

my_sentences.en: I've been looking for my keys all morning, but I can't find them.
my_sentences.ko: (아침 내내 열쇠를 찾고 있는데, 찾을 수가 없네.)

my_sentences.en: What are you looking for in your bag?
my_sentences.ko: (가방에서 뭐 찾아?)

my_sentences.en: I finally found the document I was looking for.
my_sentences.ko: (찾고 있던 서류를 마침내 발견했어.)

my_sentences.en: Help me look for my glasses, please.
my_sentences.ko: (내 안경 찾는 것 좀 도와줘.)

my_sentences.en: Did you find what you were looking for?
my_sentences.ko: (찾고 있던 거 찾았어?)

my_sentences.en: What does it look like? / It's about this big
my_sentences.ko: 외형이나 생김새를 물을 때, 그리고 손짓과 함께 크기나 모양을 대략 설명할 때 유용합니다.
bold_words: What does it look like? / It's about this big

my_sentences.en: What does your new car look like?
my_sentences.ko: (너 새 차 어떻게 생겼어?)
bold_words: What does your new car look like?

my_sentences.en: The box is about this big, so it won't fit in the trunk.
my_sentences.ko: (상자가 대충 이만한 크기라서 트렁크에 안 들어갈 거야.)

my_sentences.en: Can you describe the suspect? What did he look like?
my_sentences.ko: (용의자를 묘사해 주실 수 있나요? 어떻게 생겼었나요?)

my_sentences.en: It's a small pouch, about this big, with a zipper on top.
my_sentences.ko: (위에 지퍼가 달린 대략 요만한 크기의 작은 파우치야.)

my_sentences.en: I'm looking for a gift box about this big. Do you have any?
my_sentences.ko: (대략 이만한 크기의 선물 상자를 찾고 있는데, 있나요?)

my_sentences.en: pay for [n,-ing]
my_sentences.ko: pay 뒤에 금액이나 대상을 바로 쓰지 않고, 어떤 물건/서비스의 대가를 치를 때는 전치사 for를 씁니다.

my_sentences.en: Let me pay for lunch today.
my_sentences.ko: (오늘 점심은 내가 살게.)

my_sentences.en: Who is going to pay for the damages?
my_sentences.ko: (손해 배상은 누가 낼 건가요?)

my_sentences.en: I already paid for the parking ticket.
my_sentences.ko: (주차 요금은 이미 지불했어.)

my_sentences.en: How much did you pay for that jacket?
my_sentences.ko: (그 재킷 얼마 주고 샀어?)

my_sentences.en: You shouldn't have to pay for their mistakes.
my_sentences.ko: (그 사람들의 실수에 대해 네가 대가를 치를 필요는 없어.)

my_sentences.en: You know what? / I bet ~
my_sentences.ko: You know what?은 화제를 전환하거나 주의를 끌 때(있잖아/그거 알아?), I bet ~은 강한 추측과 확신(분명 ~일 거다)을 말할 때 씁니다.

my_sentences.en: You know what? I think we should leave early tomorrow.
my_sentences.ko: (있잖아, 우리 내일 일찍 출발하는 게 좋을 것 같아.)

my_sentences.en: I bet he forgot about our meeting.
my_sentences.ko: (장담하는데 걔 우리 회의 까먹었을걸.)

my_sentences.en: You know what? It's not worth worrying about.
my_sentences.ko: (그거 알아? 그거 전혀 걱정할 가치도 없는 일이야.)

my_sentences.en: I bet you're going to love this place.
my_sentences.ko: (분명 너 여기 아주 마음에 들어 할 거야.)

my_sentences.en: I bet she's already asleep by now.
my_sentences.ko: (틀림없이 걔 지금쯤 벌써 자고 있을 거다.)

my_sentences.en: 5. I don't know why I didn't think of that.
my_sentences.ko: 상대방이 좋은 아이디어나 뻔한 해결책을 제시했을 때 "내가 왜 그 생각을 못 했지?"라며 맞장구칠 때 자주 씁니다.
bold_words: 5. I don't know why I didn't think of that.

my_sentences.en: That's a great solution! I don't know why I didn't think of that.
my_sentences.ko: (좋은 해결책이다! 왜 그 생각을 진작 못 했지.)
bold_words: I don't know why I didn't think of that.

my_sentences.en: Restarting the router fixed it? I don't know why I didn't think of that.
my_sentences.ko: (공유기 재부팅하니까 해결됐어? 내가 왜 그 생각을 못 했을까.)
bold_words: I don't know why I didn't think of that.

my_sentences.en: We could just take the subway. I don't know why I didn't think of that earlier.
my_sentences.ko: (그냥 지하철 타도 되는데. 아까는 왜 그 생각을 못 했지.)
bold_words: I don't know why I didn't think of that earlier.

my_sentences.en: oh, right! The spare key! I don't know why I didn't think of that.
my_sentences.ko: (아 맞다! 보조 키! 왜 그 생각을 못 떠올렸을까.)
bold_words: I don't know why I didn't think of that.

my_sentences.en: It was so simple, I don't know why I didn't think of that.
my_sentences.ko: (너무 간단한 문제였는데, 왜 그 생각을 못 했는지 모르겠어.)
bold_words: I don't know why I didn't think of that.

my_sentences.en: 6. foggy / brain fog
my_sentences.ko: 날씨뿐만 아니라 수면 부족이나 피로로 "머리가 멍하고 정신이 맑지 않을 때" 사람의 상태를 비유적으로 표현합니다.

my_sentences.en: My brain is so foggy this morning; I need some coffee.
my_sentences.ko: (오늘 아침에 머리가 너무 멍해서 커피가 좀 필요해.)

my_sentences.en: I've had severe brain fog since I got sick.
my_sentences.ko: (아프고 난 뒤로 계속 머리에 안개가 낀 것처럼 멍해.)

my_sentences.en: Lack of sleep always makes me feel foggy the next day.
my_sentences.ko: (수면 부족은 다음 날 항상 정신을 멍하게 만든다.)

my_sentences.en: Sorry, I didn't catch that. My head is a little foggy today.
my_sentences.ko: (미안, 잘 못 들었어. 오늘 머리가 좀 멍하네.)

my_sentences.en: After working for ten hours straight, my thinking got completely foggy.
my_sentences.ko: (10시간 연속으로 일했더니 머리가 완전히 멍해졌다.)
